purpose: Re-sweep the JANUS nuclear/UAP lineage together with the strongest currently accessible official, archival, peer-reviewed, open-data, and contested research sources; expand the graph maximally while preserving positive, negative, contradictory, and unresolved evidence separately.

internal_janus_lineage.current_read: POSS-I nuclear presence association is schedule-confounded in the dense open S0 cohort; no robust positive conditional rate signal; Blue Book exact-date layer shows no positive STARLIKE nuclear specificity; no common external trigger admitted.
UAP-nuclear association remains open and requires exposure-normalized reanalysis; quantum branching/fission ontology is not an observed UAP mechanism.

internal_janus_lineage.warning: Its expert likelihoods and strong labels predate current corrective controls and must not override them.

external_source_graph.title: NARA Record Group 615: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection
external_source_graph.observed: NARA is receiving rolling digital UAP records from federal agencies; current listed agencies include NRC, FAA, ODNI, OSD, NSA, State, FBI, Air Force, and CBP.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Canonical discovery/provenance layer; inclusion is not validation of extraordinary origin.

external_source_graph.title: NARA UAP bulk downloads
external_source_graph.observed: NARA exposes bulk electronic records including the NRC UAP-related series, FAA, ODNI and OSD, plus historical Project Blue Book and Air Intelligence collections.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Machine-ingestible future denominator and source-validation path.

external_source_graph.title: PURSUE Department of Energy records
external_source_graph.observed: Five DOE records are publicly indexed: Enhanced Pantex Imagery; James Tuck correspondence; Pajarito Astronomers invitation; Los Alamos Conference on Aerial Phenomena 1949; Pantex Unidentified Object Incident Report 2015.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Directly expands nuclear-site provenance beyond retrospective case lists.

external_source_graph.title: DOE-UAP-D005 Pantex Unidentified Object Incident Report, 2015
external_source_graph.observed: Official PURSUE index establishes the DOE incident record. Public document transcriptions describe Ground Surveillance Radar detection, Protective Force response, visual pursuit and imagery analysis of an unidentified slow-moving object near Pantex.
external_source_graph.next_forensic_gate: Bind the original D005/D001 PDFs, radar frames, image-processing provenance, wind and known UAS/balloon controls into a dedicated case audit.

external_source_graph.title: DOE-UAP-D004 Los Alamos Conference on Aerial Phenomena, 1949
external_source_graph.observed: PURSUE indexes a 1949 Los Alamos aerial-phenomena conference. The surviving conference record concerns repeated green-fireball observations and competing hypotheses; no unique extraordinary attribution was established.

external_source_graph.title: DOE-UAP-D002 James Tuck Correspondence
external_source_graph.observed: Released correspondence preserves retrospective descriptions of green-light sightings near Los Alamos and points to Protective Force logs as the claimed contemporaneous record source.
external_source_graph.limitation: The correspondence itself is retrospective; the referenced security logs remain the higher-value target.

external_source_graph.title: AARO FY2024 Consolidated Annual Report
external_source_graph.observed: AARO received 18 reports near U.S. nuclear infrastructure, weapons and launch sites from nuclear-security/regulatory authorities; those authorities categorized all 18 as UAS. The report includes a recovered crashed UAS at D.C. Cook and repeated UAS flyovers at BWXT Lynchburg.
external_source_graph.importance: Demonstrates that nuclear-site aerial-security reports can be numerous while explicitly not classified as UAP.

external_source_graph.title: AARO FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report
external_source_graph.observed: AARO's official index lists the FY2025 report added 2026-07-20. Report text states 50 NNSA/NRC UAS incidents near nuclear infrastructure/weapons/launch sites, +177.8% from 18 in FY2024; none were reported as UAP; 47 occurred between 1700 and 0500 local and quadcopters were the most reported morphology.
external_source_graph.importance: A critical negative control against treating every nuclear-site aerial incursion as UAP.

external_source_graph.title: NRC Drones and Nuclear Power Plant Security
external_source_graph.observed: NRC states commercial UAS availability has produced numerous sightings near critical infrastructure and that regulations were updated in 2024 to require nuclear power plant licensees to report drone sightings.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Reporting-policy change point: modern raw counts across 2024 must not be interpreted without policy normalization.

external_source_graph.title: NASA UAP Independent Study Final Report
external_source_graph.observed: NASA emphasizes calibration, sensor metadata, multiple well-calibrated sensors, multispectral/hyperspectral data and clear evidence thresholds; apparent UAP can become sensor artifacts after calibration/metadata review.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Direct support for JANUS Representation Contract and detector-source separation.

external_source_graph.title: An environmental analysis of public UAP sightings and sky view potential
external_source_graph.observed: Over 98,000 public reports (2001-2020) show reporting covaries with sky-view opportunity, air traffic and military activity; authors explicitly frame opportunity-to-see as an important explanatory layer.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Strong confound model for spatial nuclear-site comparisons.

external_source_graph.title: Spatial Point Pattern Analysis of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in France
external_source_graph.observed: In an inhomogeneous spatial Poisson model, population density, factories with nuclear risk/contaminated land, and moisture were significant covariates of French UAP intensity; residual hotspots remained.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Independent non-U.S. spatial association worth prospective replication with modern reporting/opportunity controls.

external_source_graph.title: UAP Pattern Recognition Study 1945-1975 US Military Atomic Warfare Complex
external_source_graph.observed: Open report and spreadsheet contain 590 selected historical UAP reports and compare atomic production/assembly/stockpile/deployment sites against civilian and non-atomic military controls; authors report elevated activity at atomic-site classes, especially a 1948-1952 window.
external_source_graph.limitation: Selected-source historical incident compilation; observation opportunity, archival completeness, reporting intensity and site-security differences remain major confound targets.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Rich case/location dataset suitable for independent denominator-aware reanalysis.

external_source_graph.title: UAP Indications Analysis 1945-1975 United States Atomic Warfare Complex
external_source_graph.observed: Peer-reviewed successor interprets patterns in the SCU historical case corpus using scenario indicators.
external_source_graph.boundary: Scenario ranking is downstream of the selected incident corpus and must not be treated as independent confirmation of the underlying association.

external_source_graph.title: Bruehl & Villarroel 2025 POSS-I nuclear/UAP association
external_source_graph.observed: Authors report transient presence 45% more likely within +/-1 day of nuclear testing (p=.008), strongest at +1 day, and an 8.5% transient-count increase per additional UAP report on transient-positive days.
external_source_graph.boundary: Authors state association does not establish causality; later work disputes dataset and schedule interpretation.

external_source_graph.title: Watters et al. 2026 Critical Evaluation
external_source_graph.observed: The critique reports that the nuclear-test timing correlation becomes insignificant after normalization by observation days and is almost determined by the Palomar observing schedule; it also raises dataset-definition, star, scan-artifact and plate-defect concerns.
external_source_graph.topa_relation: Converges strongly with JANUS JPFM-2E schedule-confound result.

external_source_graph.title: Villarroel et al. response to Watters et al.
external_source_graph.observed: Authors argue the critique uses a reduced heterogeneous subset, conflates object-level validation with ensemble inference, is underpowered for some endpoints, and does not invalidate the original findings.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Preserves the live methodological dispute rather than prematurely selecting one side.

external_source_graph.title: Doherty 2026 Independent Replication
external_source_graph.observed: Using the original author-provided dataset, the preprint reproduces RR=1.45, reports permutation p=.006 and related Earth-shadow findings.
external_source_graph.boundary: Independent analysis of the original dataset is not an independent dataset; dataset dependence remains central.

external_source_graph.title: NARA Project Blue Book records
external_source_graph.observed: Blue Book case, administrative, OSI, photographic, motion-picture and sound records are declassified and available; NARA bulk downloads now expose large machine-readable collections.
external_source_graph.topa_value: Primary-source validation path for historical nuclear-site case claims and for JANUS's reconstructed public mirror.

evidence_channel_separation.C1_NUCLEAR_SITE_SECURITY_INCURSION: Modern UAS/unknown-object security records such as Pantex and NRC/NNSA reporting.
evidence_channel_separation.C2_HISTORICAL_NUCLEAR_LAB_AERIAL_REPORTI: Los Alamos green-fireball conference and associated records.
evidence_channel_separation.C3_NUCLEAR_TEST_TEMPORAL_CORRELATION_PHO: POSS-I statistical branch; currently dataset- and observation-schedule-contested.
evidence_channel_separation.C4_NUCLEAR_COMPLEX_SPATIAL_REPORT_ASSOCI: French spatial study and SCU historical site corpus.
evidence_channel_separation.C5_CLAIMED_WEAPONS_SYSTEM_INTERFERENCE: Malmstrom/ICBM and similar testimony/document branches; requires direct maintenance/event records and causal attribution control.
evidence_channel_separation.C6_MODERN_NUCLEAR_UAS_BASELINE: FY24/FY25 NNSA/NRC reports explicitly classified as UAS, not UAP.
evidence_channel_separation.C7_DETECTOR_AND_REPORTING_OPPORTUNITY: NASA calibration/metadata, environmental sighting opportunity, observation schedules and reporting-policy changes.
evidence_channel_separation.C8_ORIGIN_AND_AGENCY: Nonhuman/foreign/black-project/exotic-mechanism hypotheses; not inferable directly from C1-C7.

conceptual_reporting_model.use: Forces every future site/time correlation to model opportunity, policy and sensor/classifier changes before interpretation.

strongest_positive_evidence_after_sweep: There are genuine official records of unknown or initially unidentified aerial objects/phenomena at or near nuclear laboratories/facilities, including Los Alamos historical records and Pantex 2015.
Independent spatial/historical research corpora have reported statistical clustering/association with nuclear-risk or atomic-complex sites.
The 2025 peer-reviewed Palomar study reports a nuclear-test/transient temporal association, and an independent analysis of the same original dataset reproduces it.
strongest_counterevidence_or_controls: JANUS open POSS-I reconstruction and the accepted 2026 Watters et al. critique identify observation-schedule confounding and no robust positive conditional rate signal.
JANUS exact-date Blue Book control does not reproduce positive nuclear STARLIKE specificity and demonstrates a clear non-nuclear baseline.
AARO FY24 and FY25 nuclear-site reports provide a large modern aerial-incursion baseline explicitly categorized as UAS rather than UAP.
NRC changed drone reporting requirements in 2024, creating a policy-driven discontinuity in modern nuclear-site counts.
NASA emphasizes that sparse metadata and sensor artifacts can prevent reliable physical interpretation.

dark_nodes_and_open_gates.question: Can the 2015 Pantex object be identified from original radar/video/image evidence, wind, trajectory and UAS/balloon controls?
Can the contemporaneous Protective Force logs referenced in later correspondence be located and matched to the 1948-1951 sightings?
Which results survive on independently reconstructed, plate-validated datasets with observation-opportunity normalization?
Do atomic-site excesses survive a complete opportunity denominator, archival completeness model, site security/reporting intensity and matched non-nuclear high-security controls?
Does the 2015 France nuclear-risk covariate survive modern GEIPAN data and explicit sky-view/reporting/site-density controls?
Can claimed ICBM/interference cases be bound to contemporaneous technical logs, electrical fault records and independent sensor evidence rather than retrospective testimony alone?
Ingest NARA RG615 NRC bulk records and build event-level UAS/UAP/security taxonomy with reporting-policy timestamps.

TOPA-N2: Pantex D005/D001 forensic bundle with original PDF pages, radar/image chain, trajectory, meteorology and UAS/balloon controls.
TOPA-N3: Los Alamos 1949/1948-1951 primary-source graph and targeted search for Protective Force logs.
TOPA-N4: prospective reanalysis of France/GEIPAN spatial nuclear-risk association on current dataset with opportunity covariates.
TOPA-N5: denominator-aware reanalysis of SCU 590-event atomic-complex dataset using matched high-security non-nuclear sites and time-varying archive/reporting opportunity.
TOPA-N6: three-representation Palomar benchmark: original author dataset, vetted critique dataset, JANUS open reconstruction; never pool them as one sample.
TOPA-N7: modern 2023-2026 nuclear-site UAS baseline with NRC 2024 reporting-rule change treated as explicit policy intervention.
canonical_seal: THE NUCLEAR-UAP QUESTION GOT LARGER, NOT SIMPLER. OFFICIAL RECORDS CONFIRM THAT UNIDENTIFIED OR AERIAL-SECURITY EVENTS HAVE OCCURRED AROUND NUCLEAR SITES, WHILE MODERN OFFICIAL DATA ALSO SHOW A LARGE DRONE BASELINE AND STRONG REPORTING-POLICY EFFECTS. THE PALOMAR SIGNAL IS A LIVE DATASET/EXPOSURE DISPUTE, NOT A SETTLED NUCLEAR EFFECT. PRESERVE EVERY WITNESS, MODEL THE DETECTOR, MODEL THE DENOMINATOR, AND DO NOT LET NUCLEAR CONTEXT SILENTLY BECOME NUCLEAR CAUSATION.
